pi_tau_policy.dyadic_effect_summary: Writing R_tau(z) = (2z - 1)*tau^{-2z}*zeta(2z) removes the 2^{2z} dyadic exponential factor from Riemann's functional equation zeta(2z) = 2*tau^{2z-1}*sin(tau*z/2)*Gamma(1-2z)*zeta(1-2z) and eliminates the 4^{-z} prefactor in K_0(z) = Gamma(2z+1)*cos(tau*z/2)*R_tau(z), changing only O(n) exponential scales while leaving the 2n log n factorial budget invariant.

bernoulli_function_definition: B(s) := -s * zeta(1 - s), with zero-argument rescaled form B(2z) = -2z * zeta(1 - 2z) and B(0) = 1

primary_sources: Riemann (1859), Ueber die Anzahl der Primzahlen unter einer gegebenen Grösse
Hurwitz (1882), Einige Eigenschaften der Dirichlet'schen Funktionen F(s)
Apostol (1976), Introduction to Analytic Number Theory, Theorem 12.13

bernoulli_function_zero_mapping.theorem: For every nontrivial zero rho of zeta(s) (0 < Re(rho) < 1), the functional equation implies zeta(1 - rho) = 0, so B(rho) = -rho * zeta(1 - rho) = 0 and K_0(rho/2) = (rho/2)*(rho - 1)*zeta(1 - rho) = 0. The full zero divisors on C are NOT identical: R_tau(z) vanishes at negative integers z = -k (k >= 1), whereas B(2z) vanishes at positive half-integers z = k + 1/2 (k >= 1), and K_0(z) additionally vanishes at z = 1/2.

K0_entire_status.pole_cancellation_mechanism: In Gamma(2z+1)*cos(tau*z/2)*R_tau(z), the simple poles of Gamma(2z+1) at half-integers z = -k - 1/2 (k >= 0) are cancelled by the simple zeros of cos(tau*z/2), while the simple poles of Gamma(2z+1) at negative integers z = -k (k >= 1) are cancelled by the trivial zeros of zeta(2z) in R_tau(z).

K0_nontrivial_zero_preservation.formula: For every nontrivial zero rho of zeta(s), K_0(rho / 2) = (rho / 2) * (rho - 1) * zeta(1 - rho) = 0

K0_sample_denominator_growth.exact_D_n_B_formula: D_n^B = lcm_{0 <= m <= n} den(B_{2m}) = prod_{p <= 2n + 1} p = exp(vartheta(2n + 1))
K0_sample_denominator_growth.exact_D_n_K0_formula: D_n^{K_0} = lcm_{0 <= m <= n} den(K_0(m)) = 2 * prod_{p <= 2n + 1} p = 2 * exp(vartheta(2n + 1))
K0_sample_denominator_growth.asymptotic_log_D_n: log D_n^{K_0} = vartheta(2n + 1) + log(2) = 2n + o(n) = O(n)

gamma_ratio_family.definition: B_q(z) := K_0(z) / Gamma(z + 1)^q = z * (2z - 1) * zeta(1 - 2z) / Gamma(z + 1)^q

gamma_ratio_sample_growth_theorem.q_eq_2_exact_exponential_scale: |B_2(m)| = (2m - 1) * binom(2m, m) * tau^{-2m} * zeta(2m) ~ (2 * sqrt(m) / sqrt(pi)) * pi^{-2m}

phase_diagram.q_3: superfactorial decay ~ exp(-m log m + O(m)), R_OGF = +infty (entire order 1)
phase_diagram.q_4: superfactorial decay ~ exp(-2m log m + O(m)), R_OGF = +infty (entire order 1/2)

gamma_ratio_denominator_bounds.theorem_statement: For every integer q >= 0 and all n >= 3, the sample denominator LCM D_{q,n} := lcm_{0 <= m <= n} den(B_q(m)) satisfies the unconditional two-sided bound: q * log(n!) + sum_{3 <= p <= n} (1 - q * floor(log_p n)) * log(p) <= log D_{q,n} <= q * log(n!) + vartheta(2n + 1) + log(2), and hence log D_{q,n} = q * n * log(n) + O_q(n).
gamma_ratio_denominator_bounds.irregular_prime_immunity_proof: For any odd prime 3 <= p <= n, let d_p = (p - 1)/2 <= (n - 1)/2 and K_p = floor(n / d_p) >= 2. Among the two consecutive integers {K_p, K_p - 1}, at least one k_p satisfies k_p != -1 (mod p). Setting m_p = k_p * d_p in [n - p + 2, n], we have: (1) (p - 1) | 2*m_p, so by von Staudt-Clausen v_p(B_{2*m_p}) = -1 (hence p divides the denominator of B_{2*m_p} and CANNOT divide its numerator, completely eliminating irregular-prime numerator cancellation!); (2) 2*m_p - 1 = k_p*(p - 1) - 1 == -(k_p + 1) != 0 (mod p), so v_p(2*m_p - 1) = 0; (3) therefore v_p(den(B_q(m_p))) = 1 + q * v_p(m_p!) >= 1 + q * (v_p(n!) - floor(log_p n)), since n - m_p < p - 1 implies at most one multiple of p^j can lie in (m_p, n] for each 1 <= j <= floor(log_p n).

q_eq_2.R_OGF: pi^2 = tau^2 / 4 (since |B_2(m)| = (2m - 1) * binom(2m, m) * tau^{-2m} * zeta(2m) ~ (2*sqrt(m)/sqrt(pi)) * pi^{-2m})

q_eq_4.R_OGF: +infty (entire OGF of order 1/2, superfactorial decay ~ m^{-2m})

positive_bernoulli_kernel.definition: P(z) := -exp(i * tau * z / 2) * B(z) = 2 * z * exp(i * pi * z) * zeta(1 - 2z)
positive_bernoulli_kernel.nontrivial_zero_vanishing: P(rho / 2) = 0 for every nontrivial zero rho of zeta(s)
positive_bernoulli_kernel.conjugate_symmetry_broken: Because exp(i*tau*z/2) = exp(i*pi*z) satisfies conj(exp(i*pi*conj(z))) = exp(-i*pi*z) != exp(i*pi*z), P(conj(z)) != conj(P(z)); its real-real sister P_cos(z) = -cos(tau*z/2)*B(z) restores P_cos(conj(z)) = conj(P_cos(z)) and satisfies P_cos(m) = |B_{2m}| > 0 (m >= 1) and P_cos(rho/2) = 0.

positive_moment_integral.ibp_squared_kernel_identity: (-1)^{m+1} * B_{2m} = 2 * tau * int_0^infty x^{2m} * (exp(tau * x) / (exp(tau * x) - 1)^2) dx  (m >= 1)
positive_moment_integral.boundary_term_verification: Integrating u = -2 / (exp(tau * x) - 1), dv = 2 * m * x^{2m - 1} dx gives [ -2 * x^{2m} / (exp(tau * x) - 1) ]_0^infty = 0 for all m >= 1 since x^{2m}/(tau*x) = O(x^{2m-1}) -> 0 at x -> 0+.

stieltjes_measure.positive_stieltjes_measure_tau: mu_m = int_0^infty y^m d nu_tau(y), where d nu_tau(y) = (tau * sqrt(y) / (4 * sinh^2(tau * sqrt(y) / 2))) dy on (0, infty)
stieltjes_measure.positive_stieltjes_measure_pi: mu_m = int_0^infty y^m d nu_pi(y), where d nu_pi(y) = (pi * sqrt(y) / (2 * sinh^2(pi * sqrt(y)))) dy on (0, infty)
stieltjes_measure.carleman_determinacy: mu_m ~ 4*sqrt(pi*m)*(m / (pi*e))^{2m+2} => mu_m^{-1/(2m)} ~ pi*e / m => sum_{m=1}^infty mu_m^{-1/(2m)} = +infty (Carleman determinate Stieltjes moment sequence)

bernoulli_hankel_determinants.asymptotic_log_H_n_B: log H_n^B = 2 * n^2 * log(n) - (3 + 2*log 2) * n^2 + O(n * log n) -> +infty

bernoulli_hankel_positivity.proof_method: Gram matrix of linearly independent powers {1, y, ..., y^{n-1}} with respect to positive Stieltjes measure d nu_tau(y) on (0, infty), plus explicit Carlitz-Touchard rational product formula.

bernoulli_argument_coupling_status.firewall_explanation: The Stieltjes moment sequence mu_m = |B_{2m+2}| = int_0^infty y^m d nu_tau(y) generates the asymptotic Stieltjes continued fraction for the trigamma/polygamma generating function S_B(w) = int_0^infty d nu_tau(y) / (w - y) ~ sum_{m=0}^infty |B_{2m+2}| / w^{m+1} as |w| -> infty. Here w is the Laplace/Stieltjes transform dual variable to the integration variable y = x^2, NOT the Mellin argument z of P(z) = -exp(i*tau*z/2)*B(z). In particular, P(rho_1/2) = 0 is a point zero in the Mellin index variable z (measuring a complex-exponent moment int_0^infty y^{rho_1/2 - 1} d nu_tau(y)), whereas the orthogonal polynomials P_n^B(X) are polynomials in the integration variable X = y on (0, infty) whose zeros all lie on (0, infty) and whose evaluations at X = rho_1, gamma_1, or alpha_1 diverge super-factorially.

orthogonal_polynomial_route.definition: Monic orthogonal polynomials P_n^B(X) with respect to d nu_tau(X) on (0, infty): int_0^infty P_m^B(X) P_n^B(X) d nu_tau(X) = (H_{n+1}^B / H_n^B) delta_{m,n}
orthogonal_polynomial_route.zeros_location: All n zeros y_{n,1} < ... < y_{n,n} of P_n^B(X) are real, simple, and strictly positive on (0, infty), with largest zero scaling like Theta(n^2)

stieltjes_pade_route.stieltjes_transform_definition: S_B(w) := int_0^infty d nu_tau(y) / (w - y) ~ sum_{m=0}^infty |B_{2m+2}| / w^{m+1}  (|w| -> infty)
stieltjes_pade_route.exact_closed_form: S_B(w) = 1 + 1/(2*sqrt(-w)) - sqrt(-w)*psi'(sqrt(-w))  for w in C \ [0, infty) with Re(sqrt(-w)) > 0
stieltjes_pade_route.exact_analytic_identification: By Binet's integral for the trigamma function psi'(z) at z = sqrt(-w) (Re(z) > 0, z^2 = -w), S_B(w) = int_0^infty d nu_tau(y) / (w - y) = 1 + 1/(2*sqrt(-w)) - sqrt(-w)*psi'(sqrt(-w)), so the [n-1 / n] Padé approximants Q_{n-1}^B(w) / P_n^B(w) converge to the trigamma Stieltjes transform in w on C \ [0, infty), and have NO algebraic or functional relation to B(z) = -2z*zeta(1-2z), zeta(z), or R_tau(z) at the Mellin zero argument.

windowed_factorial_multiplier.definition: E_n(z) = sum_{k=0}^n (Delta^k E(0) / k!) * (z)_k in Q[z] with E_n(m) = (2m)! for 0 <= m <= n, F_n(z) = E_n(z) * R_tau(z)
windowed_factorial_multiplier.zero_preservation: F_n(alpha_1) = E_n(alpha_1) * R_tau(alpha_1) = 0 and F_n(m) = (-1)^{m+1} * ((2m - 1)/2) * B_{2m} for 0 <= m <= n
windowed_factorial_multiplier.height_and_evaluation_scaling: Because E_n(n) = (2n)!, the top Newton difference Delta^n E(0) ~ (2n)! forces the leading coefficient Delta^n E(0) / n! ~ (2n)! / n! = exp(2n log n - n log n + O(n)) = exp(n log n + O(n)), and primitive clearing produces log H(tilde{E}_n) ~ 2n log n and log|tilde{E}_n(alpha_1)| ~ 2n log n -> +infty.

rational_height_conservation.p_adic_valuation_theorem: Let a_m = A_m / D_m (gcd(A_m, D_m) = 1) and e_m = P_m / Q_m (gcd(P_m, Q_m) = 1) be reduced rationals with product f_m = e_m * a_m = (P_m * A_m) / (Q_m * D_m). Since gcd(A_m, D_m) = 1, any prime power p^r dividing D_m that does not divide den(f_m) must divide P_m; hence for every prime p, v_p(P_m) >= v_p(D_m) - v_p(den(f_m)). Summing v_p(.) * log(p) over all p | D_m yields log|P_m| >= log(D_m) - log(den(f_m)).
rational_height_conservation.application_to_R_tau: For a_m = R_tau(m), log(D_m) = 2m*log(m) + O(m). Any multiplier sequence e_m = E(m) that reduces the sample denominator to log(den(f_m)) = O(m) MUST satisfy log|P_m| >= 2m*log(m) - O(m), forcing either factorial sample growth |f_m| ~ exp(2m log m) (Route A, K_0) or factorial polynomial coefficient height log H(tilde{E}_n) >= 2n*log(n) - O(n) (Route C, windowed multiplier E_n).

borel_transform_route.egf_radius_of_convergence: tau = 2 * pi (poles of coth(x/2) at x = +- i * tau * k, k >= 1)
borel_transform_route.zero_argument_firewall: Dividing B_{2m} by (2m)! in the Borel/EGF series sum B_{2m} x^{2m}/(2m)! = (x/2)coth(x/2) Simply undo the Gamma-reflection and returns to the Taylor coefficients of R_tau(m), while replacing the zeta-zero argument z = rho/2 (which enters as the Mellin exponent of x^{2z-1} in int_0^infty x^{2z-1}/(e^{tau x}-1) dx) by the dummy EGF power-series variable x. Polynomial approximations in x do NOT produce polynomials in rho_1 or gamma_1.

interpolation_basis_audit.polya_ostrowski_lattice_theorem: By Pólya's theorem (1919) on integer-valued polynomials Int(Z) = {P in Q[z] : P(Z) subset Z}, the binomial polynomials binom(z, k) = z(z-1)...(z-k+1)/k! (0 <= k <= n) form a Z-module basis for all degree-<=n polynomials taking integer values on {0, 1, ..., n}. Consequently, ANY degree-n polynomial P_n(z) in Q[z] determined by rational samples P_n(m) = f(m) on {0, 1, ..., n} has leading coefficient [z^n] P_n(z) = (Delta^n f(0)) / n!, and on even nodes {0, 2, ..., 2n} has leading coefficient [s^n] P_n(s) = (Delta^n f(0)) / (2^n * n!). Central factorial bases and Lagrange bases span the EXACT same polynomial interpolation space and therefore produce the IDENTICAL unique interpolating polynomial P_n with the identical primitive integer norm polynomial tilde{Q}_n(Y)!

bases_compared.ordinary_newton_falling_factorial: binom(z, k) = (z)_k / k! — spans unique interpolant on {0, ..., n}; top denominator n!
bases_compared.central_factorial_basis: z * prod_{j=1}^{k-1} (z^2 - j^2) / (2k-1)! — spans unique interpolant on symmetric integer window; top denominator (2k-1)!
bases_compared.even_node_newton_basis: binom(s/2, k) = s(s-2)...(s-2k+2) / (2^k k!) — spans unique interpolant on {0, 2, ..., 2n}; top denominator 2^n n!
bases_compared.lagrange_basis_on_even_nodes: prod_{j != m} ((s - 2j)/(2m - 2j)) — identical unique interpolant on {0, 2, ..., 2n}; denominator 2^n m!(n-m)!
bases_compared.polya_bhargava_integer_valued_basis: Z-basis binom(z, k) of Int(Z); requires n! clearing to convert to Z[z]
bases_compared.mahler_p_adic_basis: Converges in Q_p under Kummer congruences, diverges in archimedean metric on C
bases_compared.hermite_coalescent_interpolation: Requires derivatives f^{(r)}(m) involving transcendental polygamma/zeta'(2m) values, failing Gate K2 (rational samples)

rho_scale_vs_half_scale.exact_algebraic_equivalence: Because s(Y) = 2 * alpha(Y) and the even sampling nodes are s_m = 2 * z_m = 2m, the even-node Newton basis element binom(s(Y)/2, k) = prod_{j=0}^{k-1} ((s(Y) - 2j) / (2*(j+1))) = prod_{j=0}^{k-1} ((alpha(Y) - j)/(j+1)) = binom(alpha(Y), k) is IDENTICALLY EQUAL as a polynomial in Y! zero_divisor_comparison.nontrivial_zeta_zero_equivalence: For every nontrivial zero rho of zeta(s) (0 < Re(rho) < 1), the functional equation gives zeta(rho) = 0 <=> zeta(1 - rho) = 0. Hence at z = rho / 2 (0 < Re(z) < 1/2), R_tau(rho/2) = 0 <=> B(rho/2) = 0 <=> K_0(rho/2) = 0 <=> B_q(rho/2) = 0.

R_tau(z).extra_zeros: {-k : k in Z_{>= 1}} (trivial zeros of zeta(2z) at 2z = -2k)

B_q(z).extra_zeros: {1/2} union {k + 1/2 : k in Z_{>= 1}} union {-k : k in Z_{>= 1}, multiplicity q}

von_staudt_clausen_denominator_audit.von_staudt_clausen_theorem: For every m >= 1, B_{2m} + sum_{(p - 1) | 2m} (1 / p) in Z, so den(B_{2m}) = prod_{(p - 1) | 2m} p is strictly squarefree.
von_staudt_clausen_denominator_audit.exact_D_n_B_theorem: For every integer n >= 1, D_n^B := lcm_{0 <= m <= n} den(B_{2m}) = prod_{p <= 2n + 1} p = exp(vartheta(2n + 1)). Proof: if p | den(B_{2m}) for some m <= n, then p - 1 <= 2m <= 2n, so p <= 2n + 1 and v_p(den(B_{2m})) = 1; conversely, for every prime p <= 2n + 1, m_p = (p - 1)/2 <= n (for odd p) or m_2 = 1 <= n (for p = 2) satisfies (p - 1) | 2*m_p, so p || den(B_{2*m_p}).
von_staudt_clausen_denominator_audit.exact_D_n_K0_theorem: For every integer n >= 1, D_n^{K_0} := lcm_{0 <= m <= n} den(K_0(m)) = 2 * prod_{p <= 2n + 1} p = 2 * D_n^B. Proof: at m = 0, K_0(0) = 1/2 and at m = 1, K_0(1) = -1/12 gives v_2(D_n^{K_0}) = 2; for every odd prime p <= 2n + 1, at m_p = (p - 1)/2 <= n we have 2*m_p - 1 = p - 2, and gcd(p - 2, p) = 1, so the factor (2*m_p - 1) never cancels p from den(B_{p-1}).
von_staudt_clausen_denominator_audit.asymptotic_log_D_n_K0: log D_n^{K_0} = vartheta(2n + 1) + log(2) = 2n + o(n) = O(n)

gamma_ratio_family_Bq.definition: B_q(z) := K_0(z) / Gamma(z + 1)^q = z * (2z - 1) * zeta(1 - 2z) / Gamma(z + 1)^q

Bq_two_sided_denominator_theorem.theorem_statement: For every integer q >= 0 and all n >= 3, the sample denominator LCM D_{q,n} := lcm_{0 <= m <= n} den(B_q(m)) satisfies the unconditional two-sided bound: q * log(n!) + sum_{3 <= p <= n} (1 - q * floor(log_p n)) * log(p) <= log D_{q,n} <= q * log(n!) + vartheta(2n + 1) + log(2), and hence log D_{q,n} = q * n * log(n) + O_q(n).
Bq_two_sided_denominator_theorem.irregular_prime_immunity_proof: For any odd prime 3 <= p <= n, let d_p = (p - 1)/2 <= (n - 1)/2 and K_p = floor(n / d_p) >= 2. Among the two consecutive integers {K_p, K_p - 1}, at least one k_p satisfies k_p != -1 (mod p). Setting m_p = k_p * d_p in [n - p + 2, n], we have: (1) (p - 1) | 2*m_p, so by von Staudt-Clausen v_p(B_{2*m_p}) = -1 (hence p divides the denominator of B_{2*m_p} and CANNOT divide its numerator, completely eliminating irregular-prime numerator cancellation!); (2) 2*m_p - 1 = k_p*(p - 1) - 1 == -(k_p + 1) != 0 (mod p), so v_p(2*m_p - 1) = 0; (3) therefore v_p(den(B_q(m_p))) = 1 + q * v_p(m_p!) >= 1 + q * (v_p(n!) - floor(log_p n)), since n - m_p < p - 1 implies at most one multiple of p^j can lie in (m_p, n] for each 1 <= j <= floor(log_p n).

q_eq_2.R_OGF: pi^2 = tau^2 / 4 (since |B_2(m)| = (2m - 1) * binom(2m, m) * tau^{-2m} * zeta(2m) ~ (2*sqrt(m)/sqrt(pi)) * pi^{-2m})

q_eq_4.R_OGF: +infty (entire OGF of order 1/2, superfactorial decay ~ m^{-2m})

sign_adjusted_positive_kernel_P.definition: P(z) := -exp(i * tau * z / 2) * B(z) = 2 * z * exp(i * pi * z) * zeta(1 - 2z)
sign_adjusted_positive_kernel_P.nontrivial_zero_vanishing: P(rho / 2) = 0 for every nontrivial zero rho of zeta(s)
sign_adjusted_positive_kernel_P.conjugate_symmetry_broken: Because exp(i*tau*z/2) = exp(i*pi*z) satisfies conj(exp(i*pi*conj(z))) = exp(-i*pi*z) != exp(i*pi*z), P(conj(z)) != conj(P(z)); its real-real sister P_cos(z) = -cos(tau*z/2)*B(z) restores P_cos(conj(z)) = conj(P_cos(z)) and satisfies P_cos(m) = |B_{2m}| > 0 (m >= 1) and P_cos(rho/2) = 0.

bernoulli_stieltjes_moment_measure.positive_stieltjes_measure_tau: mu_m = int_0^infty y^m d nu_tau(y), where d nu_tau(y) = (tau * sqrt(y) / (4 * sinh^2(tau * sqrt(y) / 2))) dy on (0, infty)
bernoulli_stieltjes_moment_measure.positive_stieltjes_measure_pi: mu_m = int_0^infty y^m d nu_pi(y), where d nu_pi(y) = (pi * sqrt(y) / (2 * sinh^2(pi * sqrt(y)))) dy on (0, infty)
bernoulli_stieltjes_moment_measure.carleman_determinacy: mu_m ~ 4*sqrt(pi*m)*(m / (pi*e))^{2m+2} => mu_m^{-1/(2m)} ~ pi*e / m => sum_{m=1}^infty mu_m^{-1/(2m)} = +infty (Carleman determinate Stieltjes moment sequence)

bernoulli_orthogonal_polynomials.definition: Monic orthogonal polynomials P_n^B(X) with respect to d nu_tau(X) on (0, infty): int_0^infty P_m^B(X) P_n^B(X) d nu_tau(X) = (H_{n+1}^B / H_n^B) delta_{m,n}
bernoulli_orthogonal_polynomials.zeros_location: All n zeros y_{n,1} < ... < y_{n,n} of P_n^B(X) are real, simple, and strictly positive on (0, infty), with largest zero scaling like Theta(n^2)

bernoulli_hankel_argument_coupling_audit.firewall_explanation: The Stieltjes moment sequence mu_m = |B_{2m+2}| = int_0^infty y^m d nu_tau(y) generates the asymptotic Stieltjes continued fraction for the trigamma/polygamma generating function S_B(w) = int_0^infty d nu_tau(y) / (w - y) ~ sum_{m=0}^infty |B_{2m+2}| / w^{m+1} as |w| -> infty. Here w is the Laplace/Stieltjes transform dual variable to the integration variable y = x^2, NOT the Mellin argument z of P(z) = -exp(i*tau*z/2)*B(z). In particular, P(rho_1/2) = 0 is a point zero in the Mellin index variable z (measuring a complex-exponent moment int_0^infty y^{rho_1/2 - 1} d nu_tau(y)), whereas the orthogonal polynomials P_n^B(X) are polynomials in the integration variable X = y on (0, infty) whose zeros all lie on (0, infty) and whose evaluations at X = rho_1, gamma_1, or alpha_1 diverge super-factorially.

hankel_determinant_comparison_D_tau_vs_H.exact_denominator_polygonal_match: Notice that BOTH D_n^{(tau)} and H_n^B share the exact same Lambert-Stieltjes denominator factors prod_{k=1}^{n-1} [(4k-1)(4k+1)^2(4k+3)]^{n-k}! Removing 1/(2*(2m+2)!) from b_m^{(tau)} to form mu_m = |B_{2m+2}| multiplies the k-th Jacobi recurrence coefficient by 4*k^3*(k+1)*(2k-1)*(2k+1)^3, flipping the leading asymptotic from -2*n^2*log(n) (super-factorial decay) to +2*n^2*log(n) (super-factorial growth).

lagrange_equispaced_interpolation_audit.basis_denominator_identity: Multiplying ell_{n,m}(z) by n! gives (-1)^{n - m} * binom(n, m) * prod_{j != m} (z - j), whose leading coefficient is (-1)^{n - m} * binom(n, m) / n!. Thus clearing the Lagrange basis denominators on equispaced nodes {0, ..., n} requires a factor of order n! = exp(n log n - n + O(log n)) (or (n!)^2 = exp(2n log n + O(n)) in the conjugate-squared norm polynomial).

newton_forward_difference_bernoulli_audi.universal_primitive_cancellation_theorem: For ANY rational sequence f(m) in Q with Delta^{n+1} f(0) != 0, the two-step Newton norm polynomial Q_n^{[f]}(Y) = |N_n^{[f]}(alpha(Y))|^2 + |N_{n+1}^{[f]}(alpha(Y))|^2 in Q[Y] has leading coefficient q_{n,2n+2}^{[f]} = (Delta^{n+1} f(0))^2 / (4^{n+1} * ((n+1)!)^2) > 0, and satisfies Q_n^{[f]}(Y) >= (1/2) * q_{n,2n+2}^{[f]} * prod_{j=0}^n ((2j - 1/2)^2 + Y^2). Therefore, in the canonical primitive integer normalization tilde{Q}_n^{[f]}(Y) = M_n^{[f]} Q_n^{[f]}(Y) in Z[Y], the integer leading coefficient tilde{q}_{n,2n+2}^{[f]} = M_n^{[f]} q_{n,2n+2}^{[f]} >= 1 forces tilde{Q}_n^{[f]}(gamma_1) >= (1/2) * prod_{j=0}^n ((2j - 1/2)^2 + gamma_1^2) >= (1/2)*(1/4 + gamma_1^2)*(n!)^2 -> +infty UNIVERSALLY, independent of the sample sequence f(m)!
newton_forward_difference_bernoulli_audi.divergence_of_newton_series_for_B_and_K0: For B(m) = B_{2m} and K_0(m) = -((2m-1)/2)*B_{2m}, the top term in Delta^n f(0) = sum_{m=0}^n (-1)^{n-m} binom(n,m) f(m) has |f(n)| ~ 2*(2n)! / tau^{2n}, so |Delta^n f(0)| / n! ~ 2 * (2n)! / (n! * tau^{2n}) ~ (4*n / (e*tau^2))^n -> +infty, and the Newton series diverges for every non-integer z.

mahler_p_adic_bernoulli_comparison.p_adic_kubota_leopoldt_bridge: In p-adic analysis (p >= 3), the Euler-factor-modified Bernoulli samples c_m^{(p)} := (1 - p^{2m - 1}) * B_{2m} / (2m) satisfy Kummer's congruences Delta_d^k c_m^{(p)} == 0 (mod p^k) for (p - 1) | d, giving a convergent Mahler series for L_p(1 - s, omega^i) on Z_p.
mahler_p_adic_bernoulli_comparison.archimedean_obstruction: Kummer congruences hold in the p-adic metric |.|_p on steps d divisible by (p - 1), whereas in the archimedean metric |.|_infty on C, |(1 - p^{2m - 1}) * B_{2m} / (2m)| grows even faster (~ p^{2m} * (2m)! / tau^{2m}) and does not evaluate the complex archimedean zero alpha_1 = 1/4 + i*gamma_1/2.

norlund_bernoulli_polynomial_audit.bernoulli_polynomial_identity: By the classical Hurwitz-zeta identity B_n(x) = -n * zeta(1 - n, x), expanding around shifted nodes or in Bernoulli polynomials B_k(z) = sum_{j=0}^k binom(k, j) B_j z^{k-j} still requires Carlitz-Stieltjes moment determinants of order exp(2*n^2*log n) or factorial coefficient clearing.

riesz_gram_hadamard_kernel_audit.riesz_function_analysis: Riesz's function Riesz(x) = sum_{k=1}^infty (-1)^{k+1} x^k / ((k - 1)! * zeta(2k)) has Mellin transform int_0^infty x^{-s-1} Riesz(x) dx = Gamma(-s) / zeta(2s). However: (1) its Taylor coefficients 1 / ((k - 1)! * zeta(2k)) = 2 * (2k)! / ((k - 1)! * |B_{2k}| * tau^{2k}) are transcendental multiples of tau^{-2k}, not rationals; and (2) the zero-free/RH criterion is an asymptotic bound Riesz(x) = O(x^{1/4 + eps}) as x -> +infty (or Baez-Duarte c_n = O(n^{-3/4 + eps})), not a point vanishing F(rho_1 / 2) = 0.
riesz_gram_hadamard_kernel_audit.gram_series_analysis: The Gram series G(x) = 1 + sum_{k=1}^infty (log x)^k / (k * k! * zeta(k + 1)) approximates R(x) ~ li(x) via global explicit-formula sums over all zeros rho, with irrational coefficients zeta(k + 1)^{-1} at even/odd k.
riesz_gram_hadamard_kernel_audit.hadamard_product_analysis: The Hadamard product xi(s) = xi(0) * prod_rho (1 - s / rho) vanishes at every individual zero rho, but its Taylor/interpolation coefficients at integer nodes s = m are symmetric functions of all nontrivial zeros (involving log(pi), Euler's gamma, and transcendental derivatives xi^{(k)}(0)), not known rationals.

multipoint_pade_kernel_comparison.summary: Across 1 <= n <= 7, the divergent-OGF kernels K_0 (q=0) and B_1 (q=1) suffer catastrophic raw evaluation growth (log|Q_n(gamma_1)| > 0) AND quadratic-factorial determinant clearing log M_n ~ C n^2 log n, even though K_0 has subfactorial sample denominators! The bounded-radius kernels R_tau, R_pi, and B_2 (q=2) achieve genuine raw residual decay log|Q_n(gamma_1)| < 0, but their primitive integer clearing multipliers log M_n = log(L_n / g_n) grow far faster than the raw decay, so log tilde{Q}_n(gamma_1) > 0 and grows rapidly for all 1 <= n <= 7.

pade_asymptotic_for_R_c.hermite_walsh_contour_representation: For R_c(z) (c in {1, 4}), the multipoint Padé error on {0, ..., 2n} satisfies R_c(z) - A_n(z)/B_n(z) = (omega_{2n+1}(z) / (2*pi*i * B_n(z))) * oint (R_c(zeta) * B_n(zeta) / omega_{2n+1}(zeta)) d zeta where omega_{2n+1}(z) = prod_{m=0}^{2n} (z - m). Because the Cauchy/Laplace kernel of R_c has essential singularity exp(-sqrt(c)/u) at u = 0, raw Padé residuals decay subfactorially while Cramer/Hankel denominator clearing of A_n, B_n scales superlinearly in n log n.

pade_asymptotic_for_B2.left_half_plane_growth_comparison: Unlike R_tau(z) = (2z - 1)*tau^{-2z}*zeta(2z), which is bounded by O(|z|^{1/2}) on Re(z) >= 1/4, B_2(z) = R_tau(z) * Gamma(2z + 1) * cos(tau*z/2) / Gamma(z + 1)^2 grows like 4^z / sqrt(pi*z) for Re(z) -> +infty and carries double poles of 1/Gamma(z+1)^2 at negative integers z = -1, -2, ..., producing slower raw interpolation decay than R_pi(z) while retaining the same 2*n*log(n) sample denominator cost.

pade_divergent_carleman_audit_for_B.carleman_determinacy_of_moment_sequence: Although mu_m = |B_{2m+2}| satisfies Carleman's condition sum_{m>=1} mu_m^{-1/(2m)} = +infty, that guarantees convergence of the Stieltjes continued fraction for the asymptotic series S_B(w) = int_0^infty d nu_tau(y) / (w - y) in the transform variable w -> infty, NOT convergence of multipoint rational interpolation of B(m) = B_{2m} at the Mellin zero argument z = alpha_1.

factorial_relocation_analysis.governing_answer: YES for the sample denominator alone: Gamma-reflection B(z) = -2z*zeta(1-2z) and K_0(z) = z*(2z-1)*zeta(1-2z) rigorously reduce the integer-sample denominator LCM from exp(2n log n + O(n)) to the squarefree von Staudt-Clausen primorial D_n^B = prod_{p <= 2n+1} p = exp(vartheta(2n+1)) = exp(2n + o(n)) (`SUBFACTORIAL_RATIONAL_SAMPLE_DENOMINATOR_ACHIEVED`), while preserving exact vanishing at every nontrivial zeta-zero argument z = rho/2. NO for escaping the total factorial cost on equispaced integer nodes {0, ..., n}: across the entire Gamma-reflection / Gamma-ratio class B_q(z) = K_0(z)/Gamma(z+1)^q, the 2*n*log(n) factorial budget is strictly conserved between sample growth (2-q)*n*log(n) and sample denominator growth q*n*log(n), while equispaced Newton/Lagrange polynomial bases independently enforce the universal primitive norm lower bound tilde{Q}_n(gamma_1) >= (1/2)*prod_{j=0}^n ((2j - 1/2)^2 + gamma_1^2) -> +infty.

conditional_no_go_or_escape_theorem.theorem_name: Equispaced Gamma-Ratio & Consecutive-Newton Factorial Conservation No-Go Theorem
conditional_no_go_or_escape_theorem.exact_statement: Let F_q(z) = c^z * K_0(z) / Gamma(z + 1)^q (q in Z_{>= 0}, c in Q_{>0}) be any kernel in the Gamma-reflected / Gamma-ratio hierarchy evaluated on equispaced integer nodes m = 0, 1, ..., n. Then: (1) [Exact Sample-Growth + Sample-Denominator Conservation] By Euler's formula and the irregular-prime-free von Staudt-Clausen witness m_p = k_p*(p-1)/2, log|F_q(n)| = (2 - q)*n*log(n) + O_{q,c}(n) and log(lcm_{0<=m<=n} den(F_q(m))) = q*n*log(n) + O_{q,c}(n), so their sum equals 2*n*log(n) + O_{q,c}(n) for EVERY q >= 0. (2) [Universal Consecutive-Newton Primitive Obstruction] For ANY kernel f(z) with rational samples f(m) in Q and Delta^{n+1} f(0) != 0, the canonical primitive integer two-approximant Newton norm polynomial tilde{Q}_n^{[f]}(Y) in Z[Y] satisfies tilde{Q}_n^{[f]}(Y) >= (1/2) * prod_{j=0}^n ((2j - 1/2)^2 + Y^2) >= (1/2)*(1/4 + Y^2)*(n!)^2 -> +infty for all Y in R, because the primitive multiplier M_n >= 1/q_{n,2n+2} cancels (Delta^{n+1} f(0))^2 identically while retaining 4^{n+1}((n+1)!)^2 from the equispaced Newton basis.
conditional_no_go_or_escape_theorem.what_would_be_required_to_escape: To escape this no-go theorem, an architecture must abandon equispaced integer polynomial interpolation {0, 1, ..., n} (which forces both the (n!)^2 basis denominator and the 2n log n Stirling/Bernoulli trade-off) or establish an all-n multipoint rational/Padé cancellation where common integer content g_n in the Cramer determinant cancels the denominator LCM (which does NOT occur for 1 <= n <= 7).

davenport_heilbronn_control.explanation: The Gamma-reflection identity K_0(z) = Gamma(2z+1)*cos(tau*z/2)*R_tau(z) = z*(2z-1)*zeta(1-2z) and the factorial budget conservation (2-q)*n*log(n) + q*n*log(n) = 2*n*log(n) depend ONLY on Riemann's functional equation and Stirling's formula for Gamma, not on the Euler product. For Davenport-Heilbronn, the linear combination coefficients involve algebraic/transcendental L-function factors so rational sampling already fails at Gate Z2, while for Riemann zeta the rational Bernoulli samples pass Gate Z2 with O(n) log-denominator but fail Gate Z5 via factorial sample growth.

off_line_zero_control.explanation: By the functional equation zeta(rho_off) = 0 <=> zeta(1 - rho_off) = 0, both B(rho_off/2) = 0 and K_0(rho_off/2) = 0 hold unconditionally for any nontrivial zero (on-line or off-line). Writing alpha(beta, Y) = beta/2 + i*Y/2 makes P(alpha)*P(conj(alpha)) a polynomial in (beta, Y^2) which specializes to a 1-variable polynomial Q_n(Y) in Q[Y] whenever beta in Q (in particular beta = 1/2).
